headline: Dembélé's Masterclass Proves Too Much for Toothless Iraq
story: France seized control within fourteen minutes of kickoff, an early strike establishing the shape of a one-sided contest. Against Iraqi passivity, Dembélé and Olise exploited the flanks with ease, generating constant danger from positions Iraq's defence could not cover. A second goal early in the second half, at the 54-minute mark, reduced the match to ritual; a third four minutes later confirmed what had been inevitable since the opening quarter-hour.

France's dominance rested not on possession—49%—but on velocity and suffocation of Iraq's attacks. Eight high-press phases yielded 42 forced turnovers, setting Dembélé (8.8) and Olise (8.3) loose against a fractured defence. Iraq's four shots went unthreatened; one big chance in the 75th was squandered. For France, Mbappe's 8.3 rating reflected balanced threat, though late profligacy—three missed chances after the 59th—went unpunished only because Iraq created nothing.

keyMoment.text: An early French goal shattered Iraqi hopes of weathering the deluge to come.

home.verdict: Dominant in press intensity and personnel; survived late profligacy against non-threatening opposition.
